en: to cross over; to move on; let slide

ex.en: Let's move on to the next topic.
I'll let it slide just this once.
There's a village once you cross this mountain.

en: to overflow; to be full of

ex.en: The water's overflowing! Turn it off quickly.
It's the weekend, so the shop is packed with customers.
Our son is full of energy.

note: Honorific verbs with her: 할머니께서 주무세요 (she's sleeping).

ex.en: I'm going to my grandma's house this weekend.
The kimchi my grandma makes is the best.
I gave my seat to an elderly lady on the bus.
The couple next door is really kind.

ex.s: 저희는 결혼한 지 일 년 된 부부예요.
ex.en: We're a couple who've been married for a year.
That couple goes hiking together every weekend.

note: Casual contraction of 그 아이; for someone not present, not elders.

ex.en: What's he up to these days?
Did she really say that?
I watched a movie with him yesterday.
It's so noisy I can't concentrate.
When you drive, focus only on driving.
I'm focusing on work these days.
Where's your hometown?
I'm going down to my hometown for the holiday.

ex.s: 이 음식을 먹으면 고향 생각이 나요.
ex.en: Eating this food makes me think of home.

en: to try hard, to make an effort
note: 애써요 (으-drop). 애쓰셨어요 = 'thanks for your hard work.'

ex.en: You worked really hard today.
I'm trying hard to get up early.
Don't try so hard. It's fine.

note: 눈을 떼다 = take one's eyes off.

ex.s: 새 옷에 붙은 가격표 좀 떼 주세요.
ex.en: Please take the price tag off the new clothes.
The baby finally took her first step.

ex.s: 영화가 너무 재밌어서 눈을 뗄 수가 없었어요.
ex.en: The movie was so fun I couldn't take my eyes off it.

ex.s: 비 올 것 같아요. 우산 가져가세요.
ex.en: It looks like rain. Take an umbrella.
Can I take this?
I'll take the leftovers home.
It's finally Friday!
The bus finally came.
My cold is finally gone.
The rain has gone on for a week now.
The meeting kept going, so I couldn't eat lunch.
If the cough continues, go see a doctor.
Which brand do you like?
This brand's shoes are really comfortable.
I look at price more than brand.

note: Homonym 가정 also means 'assumption'.

ex.en: Family is the most important thing to me.
When you live abroad, you miss home cooking.
It's hard to take care of both work and family.

note: Only males say 누나; females say 언니. Also for an older female friend.

ex.en: I have two older sisters.
Sis, let's eat together later.
My older sister works at a hospital.
Have you ever been abroad?
Living abroad is hard sometimes.
This restaurant has a lot of foreign customers.
Are you really sure?

ex.s: 내일 출발 시간은 아직 확실하지 않아요.
ex.en: Tomorrow's departure time isn't certain yet.
This road is definitely faster.

note: 부탁하다 = to ask a favor. 부탁해요 = please (I'm counting on you).

ex.en: I have a favor to ask.
I couldn't turn down my friend's request.
Please carry my bag for me. I'm asking you.

note: Counter: 장 (종이 한 장 = one sheet).

ex.en: Just give me one sheet of paper, please.
Please give it to me in a mug, not a paper cup.
Please write your phone number on the paper.

note: 상담하다 / 상담을 받다 = to get advice or counseling.

ex.en: I'd like to book a consultation.

ex.s: 요즘 너무 힘들면 상담을 받아 보세요.
ex.en: If things are too hard lately, try counseling.
I had a loan consultation at the bank.
I graduated from college last year.
When do you graduate?
My younger brother graduates from elementary school today.
I shared my trip photos with my friends.
Please share that recipe with me.
I'll share my screen before the meeting.

note: 미술관 = art museum.

ex.en: I went to an art academy when I was little.
Want to go to an art museum this weekend?

ex.s: 저는 학교에서 미술 시간이 제일 좋았어요.
ex.en: Art class was my favorite at school.
I hid my kid's birthday present in the closet.
Are you hiding something from me?

ex.s: 기분 나쁘면 숨기지 말고 말해 주세요.
ex.en: If you're upset, don't hide it. Tell me.
Is this food normally this spicy?
I don't usually eat breakfast.
The original plan was to go to the beach.
What genre of movies do you like?
This singer does a lot of different genres.

ex.s: 요즘 이 장르 음악이 인기 많아요.
ex.en: This genre of music is really popular these days.
Let's go to Korea together someday.
Someday I want to open my own shop.

ex.s: 이 노래 언젠가 들어 본 것 같아요.
ex.en: I think I've heard this song sometime before.
I like fall the most.
In the fall we go see the autumn leaves.
It's already fall, so mornings are a bit cold.
Be sure to take this medicine after meals.
On weekends you definitely need a reservation.
We'll win next time for sure.
I spilled coffee on my pants.
I worked out and sweated a lot.
I cried watching that movie.
Please tell me the truth.
That rumor isn't true.
Sometimes it's hard to hear the truth.

ex.s: 표정이 왜 그래요? 무슨 일 있어요?
ex.en: Why the face? Is something wrong?

ex.s: 사진 찍을 때 표정이 너무 굳었어요.
ex.en: My expression was so stiff in the photo.
The kid's face lit up after getting the present.

note: 농구하다 = to play basketball.

ex.en: I play basketball with friends every weekend.
Want to go watch a basketball game?
My son is learning basketball at school.

note: 공기 as a rice-bowl counter is a different word.

ex.s: 오늘 공기가 안 좋아서 마스크 썼어요.
ex.en: The air is bad today, so I wore a mask.
Now that we're in the mountains, the air is so clean.

ex.s: 여기 밥 한 공기 더 주세요.
ex.en: One more bowl of rice here, please.

note: 스트레스를 받다 = to get stressed; 풀다 = relieve it.

ex.s: 요즘 일 때문에 스트레스 많이 받아요.
ex.en: I'm really stressed from work these days.
What do you do to relieve stress?
Exercising relieves my stress a bit.
I took medicine, but it actually hurts more.
The subway is actually faster than a taxi.
I tried to help but ended up ruining it instead.

note: Two different words share this spelling.

ex.en: The lyrics of this song are so good.
I memorized all the lyrics and sang it at karaoke.
My spouse and I split the housework fifty-fifty.
Thank you for coming from so far.

ex.s: 아이들이 너무 멀리 가지 않게 해 주세요.
ex.en: Please don't let the kids go too far.

ex.s: 멀리 있어서 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
ex.en: It's far away, so I can't read the writing well.

note: Toe = 발가락.

ex.en: I cut my finger while cooking.
Don't point with your finger.
My fingers are frozen from the cold.
I bought a new phone case.
Where did you buy that glasses case?
I've never seen a case like this either.

note: Not usually for a romantic partner; use 애인 or 남편/아내.

ex.en: I'm looking for a tennis partner.
I'm having lunch with my business partner today.
In class we practice conversation with a partner.

note: 연락하다 = to contact; 연락처 = contact info.

ex.en: Let me know when you arrive.
I can't get hold of my friend these days.
Please give me your contact info.

note: Body temperature is usually 체온; fever is 열.

ex.en: Please turn down the AC temperature.
What's the temperature today?
The water temperature is just right.

note: 다녀오겠습니다 / 잘 다녀오세요 are leaving-home greetings.

ex.en: I'm going to run to the restroom.
Mom, I'm back from school!
I went to Busan last week.
My daughter is in third grade at elementary school.
I met an elementary school friend for the first time in ages.
There's an elementary school near our house.
My husband is a government employee.
I'm studying for the civil service exam these days.
The district office employee kindly helped me.

note: Often in ~게 된 계기 = what led you to ~.

ex.en: What got you into learning Korean?
That trip became a big turning point.
This was what got me to start exercising.
I borrowed a book from the library.
What time does the library close?
It's exam season, so there are no seats in the library.
The cat hid under the bed.
The kids are hiding behind the curtain.
This neighborhood has lots of hidden gem restaurants.

note: Also 한국 사람, more common in speech.

ex.en: I have a few Korean friends.
This restaurant has many Korean customers.
My husband is American, and I'm Korean.

en: to fly (a kite); blow away; lose (money)

ex.en: The kids are flying kites in the park.
The wind was strong and blew all the papers away.
I lost all my money on stocks.
Time really flies.
Even as the years go by, we're still friends.
You can see the years in Grandpa's face.

note: 덜 익었어요 = not fully cooked.

ex.en: Please make it less spicy.
Today is less cold than yesterday.
The meat isn't fully cooked yet.

note: 사과 also means 'apple'.

ex.en: I apologized to my friend for being late.
Why don't you apologize first?
The staff made a mistake, so the manager apologized.
I acted like nothing had happened.
Behave politely in front of guests.
Acting is more important than talking.

note: 근무하다 = to work (at a job). 재택근무 = remote work.

ex.en: I'm on the night shift today.
What are your working hours?
I work from home twice a week.
Please fix the air conditioner.
How much did it cost to fix the car?

ex.s: 제 한국어 틀린 거 고쳐 주세요.
ex.en: Please correct my Korean mistakes.
This place is cheap. On top of that, it's tasty.
It's raining. And on top of that, it's windy.
I woke up late, and on top of that I missed the bus.

note: 이용하다 = to use (a service, facility).

ex.en: Use of the parking lot is free.
What are the gym's hours?
I use the subway often.
That drama's ending is so predictable.
It's obvious without even asking.
I was almost late this morning.

note: Art museum is 미술관.

ex.en: I went to a museum on the weekend.
The museum is closed on Mondays.
The kids really love the museum.
I reported the results to my team leader.
If a problem comes up, report it right away.
What are you reporting in today's meeting?

note: 비교하다 = to compare.

ex.en: Don't compare yourself with other people.

ex.s: 사기 전에 가격 비교를 해 봤어요.
ex.en: I compared prices before buying.
Compared to last year, prices have gone up a lot.

en: to come to mind; to rise
note: 떠올라요 (르-irregular).

ex.en: A good idea came to me!
I can't think of that person's name.
I watched the sun rise over the sea.

note: 주문하다 = to order.

ex.en: Are you ready to order?
The clothes I ordered online arrived.
My order hasn't come out yet.
Your Korean has really improved.
Your cooking skills are really good.
I want to improve my golf skills.

note: 담배를 피우다 = to smoke; 끊다 = to quit.

ex.en: Do you smoke?
My dad finally quit smoking.
You can't smoke here.

note: Same as 도대체; used in questions, often frustrated.

ex.en: Why on earth are you acting like that?
Where on earth are my keys?
What on earth is going on?
The new phone comes out next month.
This snack came out last year.
When is that game coming out?

note: ~랑/하고 친하다 = be close with ~.

ex.en: We're really close.
Are you close with Minho?
I've made a close friend at work.
Is there a convenience store around here?
Everyone around me helped.

ex.s: 길 건너기 전에 주위를 잘 보세요.
ex.en: Look around carefully before crossing the street.
Let's have dinner together after work.
I came home after finishing class.
Have you finished your meal?
Ask an expert about that problem.
Ji-woo is a wine expert.
I'm not an expert, so I don't really know.
I have a class reunion tonight.
I go to a book club every weekend.
Where is this get-together being held?
What floor is the office on?
I came to the office early today.
The office is so cold.

note: Stronger, more emotional form of 너무.

ex.en: I miss you so very much.
I was so incredibly happy that day.
Time goes by so fast.

note: Also for medical scans: 엑스레이를 촬영하다.

ex.en: Is it okay to film here?
I filmed my friend's wedding video.
I had an X-ray taken at the hospital.

note: Casual contraction of 저 아이; for someone visible, not elders.

ex.en: Who's that over there?
That's my little brother over there.
That kid is always smiling.

en: to do like this; at this rate
note: 이러다(가) = at this rate; 왜 이래요? = why are you like this?

ex.en: At this rate we'll be late. Let's hurry.
Why are you acting like this all of a sudden?
Please don't do this.

en: to write up, to fill out

ex.en: Please fill out this form.
I have to write up a report today.
I rewrote my résumé.
Please turn up the heater a bit.
I want to improve my Korean.
I'm building up my stamina through exercise.
What time does this store open?

ex.s: 집 앞에 새 빵 가게가 생겼어요.
ex.en: A new bakery opened in front of my house.
My parents run a small shop.
Don't judge people by their looks.
My team leader rated my work highly.
People rate this restaurant highly.

note: Used by parents about their own kids; 이 자식 is an insult.

ex.en: All parents worry about their kids.
How many children do you have?
The kids are all grown, so the house is quiet.

note: Lend = 빌려주다.

ex.en: Can I borrow a pen?
I borrowed some money from a friend.
I rented a car on Jeju Island.
I made a good connection on my trip.
We signed a contract with the new company.

ex.s: 동네 사람들과 좋은 관계를 맺고 싶어요.
ex.en: I want to build good relationships with my neighbors.

en: to come up; to be posted (online)

ex.en: Please come up to the second floor.
My mom is coming up to Seoul tomorrow.
A new video was posted on YouTube.

en: to grab, hold on to; to stop

ex.en: Hold on tight to the handle on the bus.
My friend held me back, telling me not to go.
I really want to seize this opportunity.
Click this button.
I clicked the link, but it won't open.
Don't click on emails you don't recognize.
Do you have a religion?
I'm not religious.
Everyone in my family has a different religion.

note: Used as 경제적이다, 경제적인 + noun, 경제적으로.

ex.en: The subway is more economical than a car.
Things are a bit tight financially these days.
We moved for financial reasons.

note: Used as 효과적이다, 효과적인 + noun, 효과적으로.

ex.en: This method is the most effective.

ex.s: 어떻게 하면 효과적으로 공부할 수 있어요?
ex.en: How can I study effectively?
Walking is effective for relieving stress.

note: 기본적으로 = basically, by default.

ex.en: I can speak basic Korean.
Basically, I eat breakfast at home.
I know how to do basic cooking.

note: Used as 전통적이다, 전통적인 + noun, 전통적으로.

ex.s: 전통적인 한국 음식 먹어 보고 싶어요.
ex.en: I want to try traditional Korean food.
Traditionally, we eat rice cake soup on Lunar New Year.
My parents are a bit traditional.

note: Used as 세계적이다, 세계적인 + noun, 세계적으로.

ex.en: She's a world-famous singer.
Kimchi is famous around the world now.
This company has become a global brand.

note: Opposite of 양 (quantity).

ex.en: It's expensive, but the quality is good.
Quality matters more to me than quantity.
My sleep quality is poor these days.

note: 투자하다 = to invest.

ex.en: You have to be careful with investing.
Are you interested in investing in stocks?
Exercise is an investment in your health.

note: 처리하다 = to handle; 처리되다 = to be processed.

ex.en: I'll take care of this.
Your refund has been processed.
How long does the paperwork take to process?

note: 성장하다 = to grow.

ex.en: Kids grow up really fast.

ex.s: 회사가 몇 년 사이에 빠르게 성장했어요.
ex.en: The company grew fast over a few years.

ex.s: 이번 경험으로 많이 성장한 것 같아요.
ex.en: I think I grew a lot through this experience.
Reading Mom's letter left me choked up.
After the movie I felt choked up for a while.
My ears feel blocked on the plane.
